about.text: Rabri, rabdi or rabidi is a sweet, condensed-milk-based dish, originating from the Indian subcontinent, made by boiling milk on low heat for a long time until it becomes dense and changes its colour to off-white or pale yellow. Jaggery, spices, and nuts are added to it to give it flavor. It is chilled and served as dessert. Rabri is the main ingredient in several desserts, such as rasabali, chhena kheeri, and khira sagara.

how.text: Milk is boiled down slowly until thick and pale yellow; the skins that form are collected and mixed back in, giving rabri its layered texture.

steps.note: Kept low for a long time in a large open kadhai.
The cream layer is lifted off as it forms and set aside.
The skins are folded back in (lachha).
